## Design

### 2026-10-21 – Oop I forgot to post it two days ago...

**2.27h**

Oop I forgot to post it two days ago...
Anyways, 2 days ago, I finished the schematic. It was fairly simple because unlike the guide, I wanted as close to a full octave range as possible - so I did 12 keys as capacitive. I then had only 3 IOs left, so I did two switches - one is an on-off-on spdt switch that can be flicked repeatedly to increase or decrease the octave on the keys, while the other simple spst switch will switch the modes of the toggle switch - so octaves, volume up or down, etc.
I hope the budget will be enough - I unfortunately don't have much time to work on it this week so I hope the microcontroller and pcb can be covered. I hope.
Today I'll finish pcb routing and start the copper and silkscreen layers.
tldr: finished schematics and choosing capabilities for midi

### 2026-10-21 – Today, I finished the PCB routings, silkscreen stuff, and refined the capacitive keys' footprint.

**3.02h**

Today, I finished the PCB routings, silkscreen stuff, and refined the capacitive keys' footprint.
I was editing the PCB routings a lot because i wanted to make sure they looked clean, so I changed some of the IO tags around so it looks much better now! I also researched a bit on overlapping routes on back and front side.
For silkscreen, I added K/DA symbols of each member - not the official symbols, but something representing each champion (fox for ahri, kaisa's diamond back thingy, akali's kunai (might change to kama b/c it looks super similar to evelynn's), and evelynn's ribbon end thingy) on the front silkscreen. On the back, I took inspiration from the example and did a word + stuff. The word, "Firestarter", is the name of K/DA's (btw this is a virtual girl group based off of league of legends) newest song. I also added flames on the top.
I'm super happy that I learned how to import photos - I was really dying in my first PCB creation with getting the silkscreens good, but now I don't have to worry about that! Also, since it doesn't have a specific reference, I can make all of these any color!
I'm also glad I learned that I could move the IOs around for better pcb routing, as well as some details for pcb routing (not too close, unlike my first project lol).
I also worked on the footprint for the capacitive keys - I didn't realize I needed to merge my key shape with the pad, so it took quite a while, a bunch of tries, searching, and moving around, resizing the stuff to finally get it right. Now, it connects beautifully!
I'm super excited to get to program this later in the week.
to do list for me: kama vs kunai choose, 3d the parts, get the hardware parts in bom to make sure, code, readme do

ADD ON I switched the kunai out for the kama and looked for parts - I'm 4.04 over :(((( and I cannot get it down...

tldr: finished silkscreen, pcb routing, capacitive key footprint touchups
